section_summary.extract_value: This section highlights the serious health risks and high prevalence of chronic loneliness among older adults in the United States, attributing it to factors like decreased mobility and loss of loved ones. It notes the limited research on effective interventions, particularly the lack of experimental studies. The text concludes by suggesting that cognitive reframing, specifically cultivating gratitude, could be a simple tool to reduce loneliness, based on meta-analytic findings indicating that interventions targeting maladaptive social cognitions are most effective.
